PREDICTION NOW RESOLVED FOR THE INTEGRATION PATH. The first dispatch recorded that VIT REFUSES to generate anything for this unit, deterministically, because TYPE(ErrorVariables) carries `CHARACTER(:), ALLOCATABLE :: ErrMsg`. That refusal was correct and is now CLOSED, in VIT (a2e2c30), additively and red-tested.

A deferred-length CHARACTER has no C type, because its LENGTH is part of its allocation: reassigning it reallocates it, and C++ cannot reallocate Fortran's storage. It therefore crosses as THREE members -- a staging buffer the populator module owns, the current length, and the writable CAPACITY -- with the reallocating assignment performed by the reverse copy. The capacity is the member that makes the field writable rather than merely readable; without it the C++ cannot know how much room it has and `ErrVar%ErrMsg = RoutineName//':'//TRIM(ErrVar%ErrMsg)` could not be translated at all. Over-long assignment is REFUSED and reported, never truncated: a shortened error message is a plausible wrong answer, the one kind a bit comparison cannot catch.

`vit analyze-types --fix character`, the remedy VIT's own message suggested, is still REFUSED and now unnecessary. It rewrites ROSCO's type definition to a fixed length, changing LEN(ErrVar%ErrMsg), which sizes avcMSG, which is Record 49. P7.

MEASURED AFTER THE FIX: `vit translate ExtController` succeeds; `vit interface` emits all five arguments over a five-argument bridge -- read attribute by attribute against the original and matching, including REAL(4) for REAL(ReKi) (an explicit kind is not promoted by -fdefault-real-8). Generated view populators are committed at rosco/controller/src/vit_{controlparameters,localvariables,extcontroltype,errorvariables}_view.f90 and compile.

Decomposing ControlParameters (214 fields) and LocalVariables (168) produced a SUBROUTINE statement 11,747 characters long; free-form Fortran's limit is 132 columns, so gfortran truncated it and reported 1,153 diagnostics, none of which named the cause. EVERY unit in this campaign taking either type -- most of ROSCO's controllers -- was outside `vit test-validate` entirely, and nothing said so. The campaign's first four units took scalars, arrays and strings and never touched a derived type, which is why it went unmeasured until here. THE GATE CAN SEE THIS UNIT. `LocalVar%RootMOOPF` is the filtered blade-root bending moment that individual pitch control and Coleman-transform flap control are both built on; the 15 moved channels are blade pitch (x3), generator speed, torque and power, and flap angle (x3). Sixth gate-visible unit of fourteen (124,353 / 389,644 / 1,857,893 / 1,592,059 / 551,278 / 128,918).

BUT THREE OF THE SIX SCENARIOS THAT RUN IT RUN IT ON ZEROS, and the red test says so precisely: it moves channels in scenarios 8, 26 and 27 and in no others. `Examples/vit_sim.py` injects a synthetic per-blade `rootMOOP` (avrSWAP(30..32)) in exactly those three of the six. Scenarios 6, 16 and 18 execute clean Filters.f90:405 108,000 times between them on a zero input, where the filter's output is zero and scaling it by 1.000001 is the identity. `evidence/NotchFilterSlopes/scenario_arguments.txt` puts the two columns side by side; they agree exactly. Hit count is not visibility (P9) -- the same shape unit #2 measured on ColemanTransform, one layer up.

WHAT THE KERNEL CANNOT SEE: five of twelve C parameters, and one whole branch. The unit has ONE call site and it passes `Damp` as the literal `0.7_DbKi`, `Moving` as the literal `.TRUE.` and no `InitialValue` at all; `CornerFreq` is `LocalVar%RotSpeedF`, a filtered rotor speed, so `CornerFreq < 0` is false in every captured case and the saturation assignment is never executed. `evidence/NotchFilterSlopes/kernel.constant-args-stub-PASSES.verify_fields.csv` is that measurement: a translation with all five replaced by literals and the branch deleted scores 14,508 of 14,508 IDENTICAL. Only the differential harness varies any of it -- and the surviving mutant was on exactly that unreachable branch.

WHAT THE HARNESS CANNOT SEE: it holds 74 of the 103 C parameters inert, all of them the other filters' coefficient arrays inside `TYPE(FilterParameters)`. A defect confined to one of those is invisible to it -- and this unit cannot touch them.

COST PAID TO REACH 1.000, and it is a finding about the INSTRUMENT rather than about the unit. One `compare_op` mutant -- `if (CornerFreq < 0)` -> `if (CornerFreq <= 0)` -- survived the inherited 4468-case corpus. It was NOT equivalent, and that was proved rather than argued: the two predicates disagree on exactly one input, `CornerFreq == 0`, they are bit-identical at +0.0 (0 of 36 draws differ) and they differ at -0.0 in `FP%nfs_b2` (36 of 36, `8000000000000000` against `0000000000000000`). It was unreachable because the corpus CANNOT CONTAIN A NEGATIVE ZERO: `_real_magnitude_ladder` and `_ladder` both end in `list(dict.fromkeys(out))` and `0.0 == -0.0`, so a `-0.0` is absorbed by the `0.0` already there. Closed by one addition, a signed-zero block appended last; the mutant now dies on 2 of 4508 cases. The sharper half, and the reason it is a finding about instruments generally: in all 36 differing draws THE RETURN VALUE AGREES, because `(+0.0) + (-0.0)` is `+0.0`. A harness comparing only the unit's result could not have killed it at any input.
